_comment: DS-A003 decrease-only parity debt, bucketed by typed owner or CSS-variable namespace. --update-baseline may only tighten existing buckets; a new nonzero bucket requires reviewed manual adoption.

_adoptions.c2-tightening-2026-09-03: Not an adoption: a TIGHTENING, recorded here because the ceilings were edited by hand. --update-baseline rewrites the file as {version,_comment,ceilings} and would have DROPPED every entry in this object, so the eight measured drops were applied literally instead: declared-but-unemitted BrandPalette 30->0 and total 53->23, emitted-but-unconsumed collection 35->24, color 5->2, listing 8->7, metric 24->9, sidebar 10->0, workspace 32->19. Every value is the gate's own measured actual, read from its 'tighten opportunities' list; no ceiling moved up and no bucket was added or removed. The C2 exact values are preserved untouched: emitted-but-unconsumed experience=1, recipe=1, total=206.
_adoptions.r1p-closure-2026-07-27: Reviewed manual adoption (R1-P closure): (a) declared-but-unemitted.BrandPalette 0->30 and total 23->53 — W-B's optional 1:1 palette capability fields (delta contract: unauthored fields emit nothing by design); (b) emitted-but-unconsumed sidebar 5->10, total 241->245 — channels previously declared-and-unconsumed inside the rottay/bithire extensions, now compiler-emitted and census-visible (transfer, not new dead surface); consumption or retirement is the design authority wire-or-retire lane. input 2->1 tightened. independent code audit ratification required.
_adoptions.mass-c3-bithire-all-2026-08-14: Reviewed manual adoption, ONE new bucket: emitted-but-unconsumed.premium 0->2. The bithire extension drain gave `--ds-premium-card-*` a typed owner (BrandChrome.premiumCard), so the base namespace now lowers through the same shared BrandPremiumCardChrome fan-out its six sibling card namespaces already used. Two of that type's fields, `glassBg` and `footerColor`, have no var() reader under ANY namespace and are already filed in governance/tokens/decisions/writers/unused/cards/index.json; the base slot inherits them. This is census transfer, not new dead surface: emitted-but-unconsumed.total MOVED DOWN 205 -> 204 in the same change, because the legacy `--ds-button-<variant>-hover-bg` alias and the legacy `danger` variant alias were narrowed to the names Core actually reads (-14), and the three banded-card channels were taken off the shared fan-out (-7). Retiring glassBg/footerColor is a contract-removal ruling on a public field and belongs to the dead-adjudication lane, not here. No ceiling was raised and no other bucket was adopted; declared-but-unemitted.BrandPalette stayed at 30 while the actual fell 31 -> 0 (EXTENDED_PALETTE_CHANNELS respelled as a static record the parity graph can read).
_adoptions.lane-a-tint-enumerability-2026-08-10: Reviewed manual adoption, same class as (b) above. emitted-but-unconsumed.tint 0->10, total unchanged at 245 (actual 205). The tint ramp was ALREADY emitted into all three vertical artifacts; setTintScaleVariables built its keys with a ternary behind an indirection, which the parity graph's keyCandidates cannot resolve, so the emitter was census-invisible. Spelling the five scale prefixes as literals changed the CENSUS, not the runtime. Evidence, stated precisely after audit: the rewrite is output-identical by VALUE — same name templates, same value template, same guards, same insertion order — and the tenant-theme digest actuals are identical between HEAD and the working tree. Artifact byte-identity is NOT evidence here and must not be cited as such: build-vertical-artifacts reads dist, dist is stale and still carries the previous ternary emitter writing oklch, so the artifacts were never produced by the emitter this change rewrites. Two of the three pinned tenant-theme digests do not reproduce at all; that failure is byte-identical at HEAD and is pre-existing, not caused by this change. Transfer, not new dead surface. Total ratcheted 245 -> 205, the measured actual. NOT a retirement candidate as filed: --ds-tint-4 is read by brand-themes/fixtures/themanagementmiami, and DS-internal read counts exclude the three apps. Retirement of any tint step is a design ruling on a closed normative scale and belongs to its own lane.
_adoptions.c2-lowering-scanner-coverage-2026-09-03: Reviewed adoption (C2, the sole productive theme lowering): emitted-but-unconsumed experience 0->1, recipe 0->1, total 205->206. TRANSFER, NOT NEW DEAD SURFACE. Both channels were emitted before this lot by `compileBrandTheme`, which was an `export const ... = (...) => {}` arrow assigned to a const; the emitter scan reaches function declarations, so the two assignments sat outside every census. C2's orchestration is `export function compileTheme(...)`, so the same two emissions are now visible -- the hooks contract gained exactly the same pair in the same lot (compilerConcreteEmissions 2249->2251), which is the corroborating measurement. The TOTAL is the measured 206, not 205+2: the two newly-visible names arrive while one other name drained in the same tree, so the net is +1. It is set from the census, never computed from the previous ceiling -- an arithmetic ceiling is a slack ceiling. That the pair has no var() reader is not a new finding either: foundation/contracts/composition/tenants/capabilities/index.ts already records --ds-recipe-profile as measured NOT reaching production on either surface. They are provenance markers published for a JS reader, not paint. Independent code-audit ratification required, as for the R1-P closure adoption above.
